method.title: How MiraiPath works — and what it will never claim
method.intro: MiraiPath is evidence-first: every important fact should be traceable to a source, scoped to the right program and year, and honest about uncertainty. This page explains the mechanics.
matchingBody: Matching is a deterministic calculation, not a black box. Your profile is compared against each program's stated requirements: academic background, Japanese level, budget, field, school type, location and timeline.
Each factor contributes visible points to a route-fit score out of 100. Missing information and passed deadlines subtract points. You can open the full breakdown on every match card.

The score measures fit with your stated profile and preferences. It is not an admission probability — admission is always the institution's decision. AI language models never invent or select schools; results come only from the structured catalog.
verificationBody: Every fact carries a verification status. "Officially verified" means we checked the institution's official publication for that program, route and academic year. "Institution submitted" means the school provided it and our verification is pending.
"Estimated" figures (like first-year totals) are computed from published components and marked as estimates. "Outdated" flags information from a previous academic year that has not been re-checked.
sourcesBody: Sources are recorded with URL, title, owner, academic year, publication date, last-checked date, and — critically — scope: which program and admission route the source actually covers.
University-wide facts are never automatically applied to every program. A business faculty's N2 requirement says nothing about the engineering faculty's requirements.
sponsoredBody: Institutions can pay for visibility (e.g. a highlighted placement). Every sponsored placement is labeled "Sponsored opportunity".
Payment never changes route-fit scores, eligibility classifications or ranking positions in your match list. If a sponsored program ranks high for you, it earned that score from your profile alone.
consentBody: Profiles are private by default. Institutions see aggregated, anonymized demand data only.
Identifiable details are shared only when you take an explicit action — requesting an introduction or accepting one — and each grant is recorded as a consent record you can review and revoke.
uncertaintyBody: Eligibility labels are deliberately cautious: "Likely eligible based on available information", "Possibly eligible; confirmation required", "Missing important information", "Current requirement not met", "Deadline may have passed".
We never display "guaranteed admission", "perfect match" or "100% success" — those claims cannot be honest.
correctionsBody: Every listing has a "Report incorrect information" control. Reports are triaged against official sources, corrections are published with an updated last-checked date, and materially affected students are notified.
outdatedBody: When a new academic year's guide is published, prior-year facts are automatically marked "Outdated" until re-verified. Deadlines that have passed are flagged on every surface where the program appears.

privacy.title: Your data, your control
privacy.intro: Privacy is a product feature here, not a policy footnote. This page describes exactly how student data behaves — and gives you working controls.
privacy.deploymentChecking: Checking how this deployment handles submitted forms…
privacy.channelProfileLocal: Your route profile, saved routes and comparisons are stored in this browser's local storage only. They are never uploaded while you browse.

principles: Private by default: no public profile is ever created for you.

Your route profile lives in your browser's local storage and is never uploaded while you browse. Only forms you actively submit can leave your device — and the section above shows exactly where they go in this deployment.
Institutions see anonymized, aggregated demand data unless you explicitly request or accept an introduction.
Every consent you give is recorded, scoped to one institution or program, and revocable.
You can export your full profile as JSON or delete everything with one action below.
neverList: No institution access to identifiable profiles without your permission.
No passport, bank-statement or immigration-document uploads — the demo never asks for sensitive documents.
No salary leaderboards and no ranking of students against each other.
No "success scores" that aren't backed by evidence.

privacy.noProfileNote: No profile is stored in this browser right now.
privacy.demoBody: In this pilot, route profiles and all matching run in your browser, and all institutions are fictional. Depending on how the deployment is configured, submitted consultation and partner forms may be emailed to the MiraiPath team or stored in a database — the section at the top of this page always reflects this deployment. A production release adds authenticated accounts, a secured database with consent rules enforced server-side, and verified institutional sources.

about.title: Why MiraiPath exists
about.mission: Help international students make better education decisions — while helping Japanese institutions reach suitable students transparently.
about.body: Choosing a school in Japan today means 100 browser tabs, machine-translated PDFs, conflicting agency advice, and requirements that differ by program, route and year. Meanwhile, admissions teams struggle to find applicants who actually meet their conditions. MiraiPath structures the facts, scores the fit honestly, and lets both sides connect only with consent.
pilotPoints: Focus: international students already in Japan, especially Japanese-language-school students choosing between universities and vocational schools.
Languages: English and Japanese now; the architecture is ready for Nepali, Vietnamese, Chinese, Indonesian and Korean.
Next markets: students in Nepal and other countries preparing to come to Japan.
All programs in this demo are fictional; the pilot onboards real institutional data with verification before launch.
